sentences.text: The species E. rapidus stood approximately 1.2 to 1.5 meters tall and possessed highly reduced wings alongside long legs adapted for running.
Its feet featured only two toes on each foot.
The genus Ergilornis was described by Elizabeth Kozlova in 1960.
Both species of Ergilornis were found in the Ergilin Dzo Formation in present-day southeastern Mongolia.
Ergilornis likely coexisted with various contemporaries including the artiodactyl Entelodon gobiensis, the mesonychian Mongolestes hadrodens, and the perissodactyl Urtinotherium parvum.
Ergilornis is now classified as a separate family, Ergilornithidae, rather than a subfamily within Eogruidae.
Fossils of Ergilornis date to the Early Oligocene epoch.
The environment where Ergilornis lived was likely a humid floodplain that was more arid than other areas in Eurasia at that time.
